title: Stream segments to the viewer without holding them whole in memory
description: The stream role reads every segment whole into memory before sending it (internal/transcode/jobs.go readSegment, io.ReadAll). A copied segment carries the file's bitrate and lasts up to 12 seconds (DOMAINS 47), so a 4K copy segment is tens of MB per request, times every concurrent viewer, and a stream pod's memory limit must be set to survive that. Send stored segments as they are read, keeping the guarantee that a cut or empty object is treated as not there yet.
acceptanceCriteria: A stored segment, init or media, is sent while it is read, on the segment route and on the offline path (segmentOffline), from a store with a local path and from one without (S3): the viewer holds the segment's first bytes while the store has not yet given the rest, and receives the object's bytes unchanged

An absent or zero-length object is not there yet: the segment route goes on waiting and asks again, the offline path leaves the request to wait for Postgres as today, and neither ever answers 200 with an empty body
A body that ends early mid-segment and that a reopen at that offset completes (DOMAINS 42), at several offsets of one segment, is sent whole and byte-identical under its Content-Length, with no abort

A segment cut short is never sent with a clean end: if nothing of the response was sent the request waits and reads it again, and if some was the response is aborted, and a later request for that segment is served whole once the object is whole

A store failure that is not 'not found' (Stat or Open: an error, a timeout) before anything is sent ends the request with an error as today, on the offline path leaves it to wait for Postgres, and starts no job; it is never taken for a segment that is not there yet

Every 200 segment response, init or media, on both paths, carries Content-Length equal to the stored object's size and exactly that many bytes; checked with a segment larger than 2048 bytes, since net/http adds the header to a smaller body by itself

An object that gives fewer bytes than the size read for it (truncated after the size was read and still short after the Reader's resumes, or a read that fails mid-body) aborts the response on both paths: the client's read ends in an error after fewer than Content-Length bytes, never a clean end and never padding

An object replaced by one of another size after its size was read is never sent as the new object's bytes cut to the old length, nor ended cleanly short: the response is aborted, or is one object whole under its own length

Every object opened for a segment response is closed when the response ends, whether complete, aborted or left by the viewer mid-segment, and a viewer who leaves mid-segment ends the read from the store

A test holds at least 16 viewers mid-segment at the same moment (each has received part of its segment and stopped reading) on copy segments of at least 16 MiB each, through the stream role's segment route and a store without a local path, and fails unless the process's peak heap growth is under the viewers times a stated per-viewer bound; the bound is at most a sixteenth of the segment and does not grow with the segment's size, so a build that holds segments whole, or reads ahead of a slow viewer without limit, fails it

docs/running.md gives the stream role's memory as a fixed base plus a figure per concurrent viewer, for JS-056's requests and limits, says the figure does not grow with the film's bitrate or the segment's length, and a test fails when the figure differs from the bound the memory test asserts

The store has Stat on both backends, in the conformance suite on POSIX, SeaweedFS and Garage: it returns an object's size without transferring its body, store.ErrNotFound for a missing key, 0 for an empty object, the new size after a replace, and refuses a key that leaves the root
A segment already in the store costs at most one Stat and one Open of the store when no body is cut, and the offline path still asks Postgres nothing

A request waiting for a segment not yet made makes no store request of any kind (Stat, Open, List) after its first look, counted over a wait of at least 5 seconds (20 of today's 250 ms polls) during which at least three other segments of the same spec are stored and hinted; it asks the store again only when a job row or a hint says its segment is stored, or once when the job it waits on is done, cancelled or has lost its lease, as today

A waiting request is answered once its segment is stored and recorded, whichever job of the spec stored it (the one it waits on, another viewer's, a helper's), for several waiters of one segment at once and for waiters on two stream replicas; with every hint lost it is still answered, from the poll of Postgres (DOMAINS 10)
